function: Learning an analog beam codebook (phase-shift combining vectors) for uplink mmWave massive MIMO under uneven user distribution, trained in a distributed way on baseband boards (pp. 1, 3, 6-7).
system: Base station with 32-antenna ULA (0.5 spacing) and analog combining, single-antenna IoT devices, uplink TDD, no RIS; mmWave band, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 12).
method: Complex-valued network with softmax and argmax layers, self-supervised cross-entropy training; distributed learning on four boards with concatenation aggregation and short global update; FPGA training (pp. 6-8, 10).
data_channel: Own generator: clustered channels, 5 paths, Laplacian AOA with 10 degree spread; 10,000 majority-area plus 300 minority training channels, 1000 test channels per area (p. 12).
test_conditions: Trained on uneven user distribution, tested on evenly distributed set; changed distribution (areas 3, 4, 8, 9) from a warm-started codebook; phase-mismatch sweep (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Traditional DFT codebook, equal-gain combining upper bound, and centralized self-supervised codebook learning of prior work [12] (p. 12).
metrics: Average achievable rate, beam patterns, gradient latency, energy efficiency, speedup over CPU and GPU, gradient error, FPGA resources (pp. 12-16).
complexity: Floating-point multiplications per channel group before and after optimization (Eqs. 36-37); FPGA gradient latency 165.6 times lower than CPU, energy efficiency 1369 times higher (pp. 11, 15).
q1_support: p. 12: "follow a Laplacian distribution with" the same mean angle and 10 degree spread, from the authors' own generator (Table I). p. 16: "involve testing the algorithm on real-world, imbalanced IoT" data is future work. No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "training a new codebook from scratch, the training process" for the modified user set starts from the codebook of the basic scenario, with new majority area 4 and minority areas 3, 8, 9; results in Fig. 6 (p. 14).
q3_support: p. 12: "the CML self-supervised solution" of prior work [12] and the traditional DFT codebook are compared on achievable rate; "DL-based method, it achieves a higher achievable rate than" the CML method. [12] is also the backbone (p. 6).
q4_support: p. 11: "multiplications per channel group before algorithm hardware" co-optimization (F0) and after it (F1), Eqs. 36-37. p. 15: "version operates 165.6 times faster than the INTEL i7-12700H".
q5_support: p. 8: "source code from prior work [45], which is executed alone" is the baseline code of [12] (GitHub link in reference 45, p. 17). p. 12: "A total of 10 000 realizations of h are generated in area" by the authors; no own code or data link.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Local models are aggregated by concatenation inside the baseband unit over Ethernet (p. 7, p. 10), not over the air, so area 7 does not apply; the learned function is the beam codebook (area 3). q1: channels come from the authors' generator following the simplified clustered model of ref. 40 (p. 4), which is not a listed standard. q2 is borderline: the adaptation to a changed user distribution is warm-started from the basic codebook (not from scratch) but its training effort is not quantified (p. 12). q3 is borderline: baseline [12] is a prior published learned codebook, but it is also the backbone of the proposed model (p. 6), so the reviewer should confirm it is not read as the same method trained centrally. q4 counts multiplications and measured FPGA latency.
